test(daemon): a test of the process is named for it, and everything else needs no build (candybar-testing-0x6u.886)
test(daemon): every daemon a run starts is recorded and judged at its end (candybar-testing-0x6u.886)

test(daemon): the in-process daemon tests run in the jest worker (candybar-testing-0x6u.1ur) (#524)

* test(daemon): the in-process daemon tests run in the jest worker (candybar-testing-0x6u.1ur)

Twenty files, and the in-process cases of two mixed ones, move onto the harness
and start no process. What stays on one is the census's process tier, the real
client's three cases, the built bundle's three, and the one drive-bar case that
runs what `pnpm bar` runs.

The running bundle's digest is an input, read once at boot, so the update notice
and daemon-stats give one answer to what a daemon is, and the notice's cases
need no build.

A real socket serves in the worker for what opens one itself, so the frame stream
and the doctor's CLI run unchanged. A bar takes how it gets its daemon. A held
clock moves the effect, click-error and warning cases off real sleeps, on a daemon
each owns, and that daemon's clients state their deadlines on it.

* test(daemon): draw-reserve stays on a real process (candybar-testing-0x6u.1ur)

Its verdict changed on CI's runner, where timing is judged: p99 57 ms in
the worker against the 40 ms constant, on the first run. The darwin
comparison that moved it reads 3-4 ms either way, and says nothing about
two cores running four workers. Process runs miss the same gate by 2-5 ms,
which is brandon-unfiled-3248.tl8u.

* test(daemon): review fixes for the move to the worker (candybar-testing-0x6u.1ur)

The deadline case goes back to a real process in its own describe: its
answer's cold first draw has to fit the draw's reserve in wall time, which
is the bound draw-reserve just left the worker for.

The timedOut case now owns the running source it depends on. With nothing
in flight the answer is written on microtasks, ahead of the overdue
backstop, so it passed only while an earlier case left a read going.

A held clock could not fail the dissolve case, so the clock now moves
between its draws. A start refused beside a live daemon hands the env
back. A stats case ties the bundle's digest to the snapshot. The config-env
file holds the update keys as `check` does, rather than arming a daemon.

* test(daemon): the backstop case goes back to a process, and the harness holds the update keys (candybar-testing-0x6u.1ur)

The running source from the last commit did not make the timedOut case
deterministic: CI's reply still beat the backstop, and it failed 2 of 6
runs here. Whether the backstop wins is decided by the loop's own turns,
so the case returns to a real process, after the deadline case as on
main, with its original config.

An in-worker daemon now holds the update keys as a booted one does, in
the one place that starts it, so the config-env file needs no workaround.
A later listen error stays loud, and /restart keeps the new bar if the
old one's stop rejects. Two comments move back beside their cases, and
the false "nothing of the first is left" comments go.

feat(carousel): the standard control names the setting it changes, not its value (brandon-menus-sjhy.vxr)

{{ carousel "apply" "open" "label" }} draws ◀ label ▶. The label is required, the neighbour ring and the themeSwitcher segment are gone, and a value outside the domain counts as the first member.
